newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba replaces veteran culture minister.
newsitem.headline: Cuba replaces veteran culture minister.

text.p: Cuba on Tuesday replaced veteran Culture Minister Armando Hart, who had been in the post since the ministry was formed in 1976, with Abel Prieto, president of the Cuban Writers and Artists Union (UNEAC).

A brief statement in the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said Hart was being released from his duties as minister and would be given duties related to promoting the life and works of Cuba's independence hero, Jose Marti.
As is usual with such changes, the announcement said the decision had been taken by the Council of State, which President Fidel Castro heads, but gave no reason.

Hart, 66, one of Castro's longest-serving ministers, took part in the rebel movement that overthrew former dictator Fulgencio Batista and brought him to power in 1959. He was a member of the Communist Party Politburo until 1991.
Prieto, 47, is a prominent member of a younger generation of Cuban leaders and has headed the UNEAC since the late 1980s. He has been in the Politburo since 1991.
It was not clear whether Prieto would continue to head the UNEAC, a key influence in Cuba's cultural life.
